ground_truth.description: DISALLOW_SUBTASK_CREATE = ['mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask'] blocks a tool that no longer exists. Task 1543 (DF-D) unregistered the add_subtask MCP tool and deleted SqliteTaskBackend.add_subtask / TaskInterceptor.add_subtask / AddSubtaskResult (see test_task_tools.py::test_add_subtask_mcp_tool_not_registered). Disallowing a tool that isn't registered is a no-op, so this guard gives false assurance that Stage-2 subtask creation is 'blocked' while doing nothing — the exact false-negative flagged for this task.

The added test test_stage2_blocks_add_subtask asserts `'mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask' in STAGE2_DISALLOWED`, which directly contradicts the repo's existing test_stage2_no_add_subtask_in_disallowed (asserts NOT in) and test_stage2_disallows_builtins_only (asserts STAGE2_DISALLOWED == DISALLOW_BUILTIN). These assertions are mutually exclusive; once integrated with the already-merged DF-D changes the test suite cannot pass — the likely source of the escalation_created event.

stage2.py adds `mcp__fused-memory__commit_planning` to its documented Available Tools list (and the new flatten recipe depends on it), but _STAGE2_PROJECT_ID_GUIDELINE's tools string in __init__.py was only edited to remove add_subtask and was not updated to include commit_planning, leaving the two tool descriptions inconsistent.
Stray extra blank line added before class TestStagePayloadProjectIdGuideline with no functional purpose.
